what_happened: Refined the dispatch's own tentative middle-ruling: the three-way deadline fork from the local-gate case (task 343) does NOT transfer verbatim to a dispatched-subagent wait, because an async Agent dispatch exposes no PID/status primitive to poll -- so the recommended rule is a flat MUST NOT on backgrounding-and-waiting, not a bounded-deadline allowance. Also confirmed the cited 17-minute 'stranding' incident was a misdiagnosis (agent was alive, actively rewriting its report) with no confirmed stranding evidence; only a separate, already-fixed fork prompt-scoping defect was real.

Plan authoring discovered two latent hazards the research report did not name: (1) lint-agent-contracts.sh Check H greps bounded-build-waiter.md for two literal strings with head -n1, so new prose in that file can collide; (2) the report's recommended citation of docs/fork-patterns.md would dangle in the deployed tree, since that file is in no extension's installed_files (grep -c fork-patterns .claude-extensions.json is 0). Both are now explicit plan constraints with per-phase verification rather than implementation-time surprises.

Observed a foreign commit (b5c5abdeb, session sess_1791767371_662b8d, 'orchestrate conclusion: channel (a) direct fixes') land mid-Phase-4 on this shared tree, touching only agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json. Confirmed via git show --stat it has zero overlap with this task's file_scope (general-implementation-agent.md, bounded-build-waiter.md, external-process-wait.md, orchestrate-state-machine.md) and no interference with the deploy-headless.sh run about to execute. Proceeded without pausing the phase, per the territory contract's non-overlap case.
